name: Pinecone
version_context: docs accessed 2026-10-24; no public Pinecone source revision claimed
summary: A managed vector and document indexing service documented around schema-defined indexes, namespaces, dense/sparse/full-text retrieval, metadata filters, and client control/data APIs; this card is intentionally documentation-only.

features.name: Schema-defined document and vector indexes
features.description: Pinecone documents two index shapes: document indexes with declared fields and vector indexes configured by dimension, metric, and vector type. The documented index schema determines which APIs and retrieval modes apply.
benefits: Makes searchable fields and retrieval capabilities explicit at index creation
Supports document-oriented and vector-oriented data-plane contracts
costs: Index type and schema choices constrain later operations
Managed service behavior is observed through documented APIs rather than inspectable runtime source

features.name: Namespace-scoped data partitioning
features.description: Pinecone documents namespaces within an index as the target for upserts, queries, fetches, and other data operations; namespaces can isolate tenants or logically partition data.
benefits: Provides an API-visible partition boundary for tenant and workload isolation
Restricts operations to a selected logical subset
costs: Namespace lifecycle and limits are plan- and service-dependent
Partitioning strategy affects query scope and operational management

features.name: Dense, sparse, and full-text retrieval signals
features.description: Pinecone documents dense-vector semantic search, sparse-vector search, and BM25/Lucene full-text search, with hybrid retrieval able to combine keyword and semantic signals at query time.
benefits: Supports exact-token and semantic retrieval in one documented search model
Allows applications to choose or combine ranking signals
costs: Embedding, schema, and scoring choices affect relevance semantics
Hybrid ranking requires explicit signal and reranking decisions

features.name: Metadata-filtered client data plane
features.description: Pinecone documents record/document metadata and a filter expression language with comparison, existence, conjunction, disjunction, and negation operators for restricting searches.
benefits: Combines nearest-neighbor or text ranking with structured predicates
Provides a stable client-facing query contract over managed index state
costs: Metadata shape, size, and supported operators constrain application schemas
The service's internal index and filtering implementation is outside this documentation-only boundary

mathematical_views.question: How does an index schema select the set of valid document fields, vector fields, and ranking operations?
assumptions: The documented schema is the authority for client-visible capabilities
The model abstracts managed implementation and infrastructure

mathematical_views.question: How does a namespace restrict data-plane operations to a logical partition of an index?
assumptions: Every operation is associated with one documented namespace target
Namespace isolation is modeled as API scope, not a claim about physical placement
Tenant security guarantees require separate service documentation and configuration

mathematical_views.question: Under what documented inputs can dense, sparse, and text signals be combined into a retrieval result?
assumptions: Each score is generated according to the documented retrieval mode
Combination and reranking policy are application/query parameters
This view makes no relevance or performance guarantee
